topIssues.title: op-dispute-mon: ability to query supernode's VNs to get output roots
topIssues.author: pauldowman
topIssues.body:
The transition period for operators that run supernodes and op-dispute-mon will require running two instances of op-dispute-mon until the output root games have finalized. Currently, dispute-mon relies specifically on cl nodes to enrich FaultDisputeGames. And supernodes only to enrich SuperFaultDisputeGames. 

To simplify dispute-mon configuration and the infra around it, it would make sense for dispute-mon to query supernode's VNs to get output roots. This way one can run a dispute-mon that specifies only supernode-rpcs to monitor super and non-super dispute games.

topIssues.title: op-supernode: VerifiedRequiredL1 uses MIN of per-chain L1s instead of MAX
topIssues.author: ajsutton
topIssues.body:
## Summary

`Superroot.atTimestamp` in `op-supernode/supernode/activity/superroot/superroot.go:74` tracks `minVerifiedRequiredL1` as the MIN of per-chain `verifiedL1` values, then publishes it as `SuperRootResponseData.VerifiedRequiredL1`. The field's docstring says it should be "the minimum L1 block including the required data to fully verify **all** blocks at this timestamp" — that semantics requires MAX of per-chain `verifiedL1`s, not MIN.

```go
// op-supernode/supernode/activity/superroot/superroot.go:74
if verifiedL1.Number < minVerifiedRequiredL1.Number || minVerifiedRequiredL1 == (eth.BlockID{}) {
    minVerifiedRequiredL1 = verifiedL1
}
```

## Impact

The challenger trace provider's `step==0` path reads `Data.VerifiedRequiredL1` and returns `InvalidTransition` if it's past the game's `l1Head`. With the MIN bug, when only one chain is unverified at `l1Head` the supernode reports the boundary super root as "fully verified" anyway, so the trace provider returns a valid `SuperRoot` instead of `InvalidTransition`. The cascade rule ("once `InvalidTransition`, always `InvalidTransition`") is violated at this index.

This produces a real challenger / FPP disagreement in production: the challenger posts a claim that the FPP would reject, opening a dispute the challenger can't win.

## Reproduction

`op-acceptance-tests/tests/interop/proofs/serial.TestInteropFaultProofs_VariedBlockTimes` and `_FasterChainB`, in the `DisputeTimestampAfterChainHeadConsolidate-challenger` and `DisputeBlockAfterChainHead-FirstChain-challenger` subtests, surface the disagreement directly. The FPP halves of those subtests pass (cascade-from-Invalid produces Invalid as expected); the challenger halves fail because the supernode returns a valid SuperRoot at trace idx `2*stepsPerTimestamp - 1`.

The acceptance tests skip the affected challenger subtests until this is fixed (look for `SkipChallenger: true` references to this issue in `op-acceptance-tests/tests/superfaultproofs/superfaultproofs.go`).

## Suggested fix

Change MIN to MAX so `VerifiedRequiredL1` reflects the L1 block that includes data for every chain. Concretely:

```go
if verifiedL1.Number > minVerifiedRequiredL1.Number {
    minVerifiedRequiredL1 = verifiedL1
}
```

(and rename `minVerifiedRequiredL1` to `verifiedRequiredL1`). Confirm by re-running the two skipped acceptance subtests and removing the `SkipChallenger` flags.

topIssues.title: flaky test: `TestTruncateDatabaseOnELResync` — CrossSafe sync timeout during setup
topIssues.author: wwared
topIssues.body:
## Flaky Test

`TestTruncateDatabaseOnELResync` in `op-acceptance-tests/tests/safeheaddb_elsync/`

## CI Link

https://app.circleci.com/pipelines/github/ethereum-optimism/optimism/121646/workflows/ce5a39a0-34f4-49e2-ac4d-73dfad0b8596/jobs/4730402

## Error

```
operation failed permanently after 30 attempts: expected head to match: safe
```

Note: `"safe"` here is `types.CrossSafe` (which renders as `"safe"`), NOT `types.LocalSafe`.

## Error Trace

```
op-devstack/dsl/check.go:26
op-devstack/presets/singlechain_from_runtime.go:51
op-devstack/presets/singlechain_multinode.go:22
op-acceptance-tests/tests/safeheaddb_elsync/safeheaddb_test.go:15
op-acceptance-tests/tests/safeheaddb_elsync/safeheaddb_test.go:25
```

## Analysis

**This is NOT the same bug as #19661** (stale engine RPC address after restart). That issue was about a connection failure (`address unavailable`) during the stop/restart phase. This is a different failure with a different root cause.

### Where it fails

The failure occurs during **preset setup** — before the test's own stop/restart logic runs. At `singlechain_from_runtime.go:51`, the preset runs an initial sync check:

```go
dsl.CheckAll(t,
    preset.L2CLB.MatchedFn(preset.L2CL, types.CrossSafe, 30),   // ← "safe"
    preset.L2CLB.MatchedFn(preset.L2CL, types.LocalUnsafe, 30),
)
```

This waits up to 30 attempts × 2 seconds = 60 seconds for the verifier node (B) to sync its `CrossSafe` and `LocalUnsafe` heads with the sequencer node (A). The `CrossSafe` check is the one that times out.

### Why it may be flaky

Both nodes are configured with `sync.ELSync` mode and a `SafeDBPath` (lines 17-18 of `safeheaddb_test.go`). In EL Sync mode:

1. The EL syncs blocks via P2P (fast), advancing the unsafe head
2. But `CrossSafe` advancement requires the **derivation pipeline** to process L1 data and the **supervisor** to confirm cross-chain safety
3. If the derivation pipeline or supervisor is slow to start, or if L1 block production hasn't advanced enough, `CrossSafe` may not advance within the 60-second window
4. This is a timing issue that would be sensitive to CI resource contention

### Possible fix directions

- Increase the attempt count for the initial sync check when EL Sync mode is active (derivation/cross-safe promotion is expected to be slower)
- Add a more targeted wait for CrossSafe that accounts for EL Sync startup latency
- Check if the supervisor is slow to mark blocks as cross-safe during initial sync in EL Sync mode

topPRs.title: feat(op-acceptance): after-chain-head tests via TestSequencer (alt to #20349)
topPRs.author: ajsutton
topPRs.body:
Alternative implementation of ethereum-optimism/optimism#20349.

#20349 ports 6 *AfterChainHead* subtests but also rewrites the existing `RunSuperFaultProofTest` / `RunVariedBlockTimesTest` Stage 1 and Stage 2 setup, and its Stage 2b's `StartSequencer → Reached → StopSequencer` dance has an unbounded race under CI scheduling pauses (a pause of any length between two of those calls produces unbounded sequencer overshoot, which `LocalSafe` then catches up to once batchers re-submit).

This PR keeps Stage 1 / Stage 2 **byte-identical to develop** (zero deletions vs develop) and replaces Stage 2b with deterministic block production via `dsl.TestSequencer.SequenceBlock` (already exposed through `SimpleInterop`):

- Stops batchers + sequencers, waits for both safety levels to stall.
- `SequenceBlock(parent = current head)` once per chain — produces exactly one block at `parent.Time + blockTime`, no wall-clock dependence, no `Reached/Stop` race.
- Iterative-convergence catch-up: extends whichever chain is below the current max, re-derives max each iteration, terminates only when *all* chain heads are equal (handles 1 s + 2 s mixed configurations and arbitrary pre-Stage-2b chain drift).
- Restarts batchers briefly to land boundary blocks on L1, validates via supernode, captures `l1HeadAdvanced`, stops batchers.
- `claimTimestamp = boundaryTimestamp + 5` — derived from settled state.

Tests 5/6 reference `boundary+2` and `boundary+3` (boundary-relative trace indices). Sequencers stay stopped after Stage 2b so no chain has blocks past `boundary`; batchers stop after submitting boundary so no L1 batch covers anything past it. The supernode returns `InvalidTransition` at those indices deterministically.

Single-file change: `op-acceptance-tests/tests/superfaultproofs/superfaultproofs.go`, +344 / −0 vs develop.

## Test plan

- [x] `TestInteropFaultProofs ×5` on initial implementation (44/44 subtests per run, 135–169 s each)
- [x] `TestInteropFaultProofs ×1` on the convergence fix (44/44 subtests, 180 s)
- [ ] `TestPreinteropFaultProofs ×5` (not yet executed locally)
- [ ] `TestInteropFaultProofs_VariedBlockTimes` and `_FasterChainB` ×5 each (still `MarkFlaky` for ethereum-optimism/optimism#19828 — confirm this PR doesn't make that worse)

topPRs.title: test(op-acceptance): drive AfterChainHead test setup via TestSequencer
topPRs.author: ajsutton
topPRs.body:
Adds the 6 AfterChainHead subtests to the SuperFaultProofs acceptance suite and converts the existing tests' Stage 1+2 setup to deterministic block production via `TestSequencer` (replacing the running-sequencer flow). Drops `MarkFlaky` on the two varied-block-time tests — the original flake (`ethereum-optimism/optimism#19828`) is no longer reachable now that `nextTimestampAfterSafeHeads` walks past no-op transitions and `TestSequencer` drives every chain to the boundary deterministically.

Two new subtests (`DisputeTimestampAfterChainHeadConsolidate`, `DisputeBlockAfterChainHead-FirstChain`) skip their challenger halves under varied-block-time configs pending op-supernode bug `ethereum-optimism/optimism#20481` (`VerifiedRequiredL1` uses MIN of per-chain L1s instead of MAX). Their FPP halves still run.

Also bumps `GossipTimestampThreshold` to 1h in the devstack p2p config — devstack chain timestamps are synthetic and can lag wallclock during long tests, so the production-default 60s "payload too old" check rejects otherwise-valid TestSequencer-produced blocks. Devstack-only.

## Test plan

- [x] `TestInteropFaultProofs` — PASS (97s) locally
- [x] `TestInteropFaultProofs_VariedBlockTimes` — PASS (100s) locally
- [x] `TestInteropFaultProofs_VariedBlockTimes_FasterChainB` — PASS (100s) locally

topPRs.title: refactor(kona): single-definition prestate build with native + Docker paths
topPRs.author: ajsutton
topPRs.body:
## Summary

- Extract kona prestate build logic from Docker multi-stage builds into `just` targets in `rust/justfile`
- Dockerfile becomes a thin environment wrapper using mise for tool versions; cannon binary provided via `docker buildx bake` named context
- Enables native (non-Docker) prestate builds for local development: `cd rust && just build-kona-prestates`
- Reproducible Docker builds preserved: `just reproducible-prestate-kona` produces identical hashes
- `cannon-builder` image reduced to apt packages only (MIPS64 cross-toolchain)
- `lint-cannon` and `build-cannon-client` use the reproducible build Docker environment via bake
- Design doc: ethereum-optimism/design-docs#372

## Test plan

- [ ] `just reproducible-prestate-kona` produces identical prestate hashes as current main
- [ ] `cd rust && just build-kona-prestates` works natively on Linux with MIPS64 cross-toolchain
- [ ] `cd rust/kona && just lint-cannon` succeeds via Docker reproducible env
- [ ] `cd rust/kona && just build-cannon-client` succeeds via Docker reproducible env
- [ ] Top-level `just reproducible-prestate` still builds both op-program and kona in parallel
- [ ] CI `kona-publish-prestate-artifacts` job works with the updated just target

topPRs.title: docs: add output→super-root upgrade tutorial (unlinked)
topPRs.author: ajsutton
topPRs.body:
Adds a new tutorial under `docs/public-docs/chain-operators/tutorials/upgrade-chain-to-super-roots.mdx` describing how to upgrade a single OP Stack chain from output-root dispute games (`PERMISSIONED_CANNON`, `CANNON`, `CANNON_KONA`) to super-root dispute games (`SUPER_PERMISSIONED_CANNON`, `SUPER_CANNON_KONA`) via `opcm.upgrade`.

Intentionally not added to `docs.json` or linked from any other page — this should land when the op-contracts/v7.x release that supports this upgrade path is ready.

Notes for reviewers:
- The tutorial assumes `OPCMUpgradeV700` (target OPCM version `7.1.17`).
- It calls out two template extensions still required before the upgrade can run: routing both `SUPER_PERMISSIONED_CANNON` and `SUPER_CANNON_KONA` from a single kona-interop super prestate (ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops#1412) and injecting `overrides.cfg.startingAnchorRoot` from TOML.
